subject: Initial token-lag probe + integration checklist for streaming pilot
messages:

Subject: Initial token-lag probe + integration checklist for streaming pilot

Hi James —

Great to speak earlier. Thanks for the run-through of Nebula's chat use case; this thread is a short recap and an actionable checklist so we can size a pilot focused on Time‑to‑First‑Token (TTFT) and streaming behavior. I captured the goals we discussed and the items we need from your side.

Recap of objectives (what success looks like):
- TTFT target: 50 ms P50, 120 ms P95 for short prompts (<= 128 tokens).
- Sustained concurrency: 80 concurrent live sessions during peak (read/write mix).
- Throughput target: support ~350 requests/minute with average 400 tokens per response.
- Streaming: prefer low-latency chunked responses; acceptable chunk cadence ~200–400 ms depending on payload.

What we need from Nebula to validate in a 2-week sandbox pilot:
1) Representative prompt samples (small set + edge cases) — see attachment: pilot-sample-payloads.json.
2) Expected distribution: typical tokens per response, percent of long (>512 tokens) replies.
3) Preferred streaming method: SSE or WebSocket? We support both; WebSocket tends to reduce TCP handshakes but SSE is simpler for browser clients.
4) Any networking constraints (proxy, MTU, keepalive timeouts).
5) Target percentiles that matter to you (we asked P50/P95 but include P99 if you track it).

Technical notes / our ask from SE (Vivek):
- We plan a staged pilot: baseline latency test (single-client), scaled concurrency run, and then production-like mix.
- We will instrument prefix caching and continuous batching to see unit-cost tradeoffs; need your sample traffic to calibrate.

Attachments sent with this email: redwood-integration-rfc.pdf (integration checklist).

Next steps / dates:
- Can you share the sample payloads and confirm WebSocket vs SSE by EOD Monday?
- I'll schedule a focused SE session (30–45m) next week to run baseline tests.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Best,

Kimberly Park

Subject: Re: Initial token-lag probe + integration checklist for streaming pilot

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items from our side:
- We can relax TTFT slightly: our business target is 50 ms P50 and ~150 ms P95 for 128-token responses. P99 is useful but not a blocker for the pilot.
- Streaming: WebSocket preferred. Most of our clients use mobile/web SDKs with persistent sockets, so avoiding chunk reassembly on the client is helpful.
- Chunk cadence: our UX team wants frequent small chunks for progressive rendering. Ballpark: 100–250 tokens per chunk every ~200–350 ms. We can provide exact numbers after consulting the frontend team.
- Concurrency/throughput: peak estimate is 80 concurrent active sessions, burst to 150 for short periods; throughput target ~400–450 requests/minute during peak.

Attachments: attaching Nebula's internal streaming requirements spreadsheet (nebula_streaming_requirements.xlsx).

Procurement note: Elena is looping in procurement; we have a standard security questionnaire to complete — I'll share it but expect some requests for logs/retention policy.

Happy to join the SE session next week. Send a calendar invite and Vivek, can you include a short checklist of tests (p50/p95 measurements, concurrency ramp, and a baseline cold-start check)?

—James
James Park
Head of Product, Nebula Health
james@nebulahealth.com

Subject: Re: Initial token-lag probe + integration checklist for streaming pilot

Hi all —

Quick technical follow-ups and draft pilot plan. Happy to run the tests during the session and share results in real time.

Pilot structure (2 weeks):
- Phase 0 (day 0): connectivity check + auth + small sample request (verify request/response shapes).
- Phase 1 (days 1–3): single-client latency profile (cold-start and warm) — measure P50/P95/P99 TTFT and first-chunk size.
- Phase 2 (days 4–8): concurrency ramp tests (10 -> 80 -> 120) with realistic token distribution; collect token cost and per-token latency.
- Phase 3 (days 9–14): production-like run with webhooks/clients to observe chunk cadence and UX impact.

Questions for Nebula:
1) Can you provide 5–10 sample prompts with the expected max response tokens and an estimate of response length distribution? (pilot-sample-payloads.json is fine).
2) Which percentile matters most to the product team — P95 or P99? We'll prioritize the one you choose.
3) Are you open to us enabling prefix caching for repeated system prompts? That can reduce token generation time for many threads.

Notes on metrics we'll capture:
- TTFT (time from request arrival at our edge to first token emitted) — P50/P95/P99
- First-chunk size and time-to-first-chunk (for streaming UX)
- Per-token throughput and GPU utilization during concurrency tests
- Error rate and tail latencies under burst

Attachment: pilot-sample-payloads.json (small set of prompts).

If James confirms WebSocket, we'll prepare a short test harness for socket-based streaming. Otherwise, we'll use SSE.

I'll bring the baseline test scripts to the session; if you want a pre-run, share access to a sandbox API key and we'll start immediately.

—Vivek
